title: Reduced base change along a geometrically reduced algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension] and let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] such that for every extension field $L/k$ the ring $A\otimes_kL$ is reduced. Let $R$ be any reduced commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $R\otimes_kA$ is reduced. Here a commutative ring is reduced when its only nilpotent element is $0$. The tensor product has multiplication $(r\otimes a)(r'\otimes a')=rr'\otimes aa'$ and unit $1\otimes1$; no finite-generation or nonzero hypotheses are imposed.

source.place: Tag 034N, lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change, statement and proof (the reduction to finite type and embedding into a finite product of fields)

proof.text: The $k$-module $A$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], applied to $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\to V/i(U)$, shows that $i\otimes1_A:U\otimes_kA\to V\otimes_kA$ is injective for every injective $k$-linear map $i$. For a $k$-algebra inclusion this is also a ring homomorphism: on pure tensors its product formula is $(i(u)\otimes a)(i(v)\otimes b)=i(uv)\otimes ab$, and it sends the unit to the unit. We will use this for subalgebra inclusions and for the embedding into a product of fields.

source.place: Tag 034N, proof, tensoring the subalgebra and product-of-fields embeddings; Tag 00I3, the injectivity observation immediately preceding lemma-limit-argument

proof.text: Fix a finitely generated $k$-subalgebra $B\subseteq R$. It is reduced: if $b^n=0$ in $B$, its image in $R$ is nilpotent and hence zero, so $b=0$. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], $B$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] to obtain finitely many minimal primes $\mathfrak q_i$, fields $K_i=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$, and the canonical ring isomorphism $Q(B)\cong P:=\prod_{i=1}^tK_i$. The localization map $B\to Q(B)$ is injective: by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $b/1=0$ means $sb=0$ for a nonzerodivisor $s$, whence $b=0$. Thus the composite $j:B\hookrightarrow P$ is an injective $k$-algebra map, giving each $K_i$ its induced $k$-algebra structure. Since $K_i$ is a nonzero field, the unital map $k\to K_i$ has zero kernel and is a field extension. If $B=0$, then $B\otimes_kA=0$ directly from bilinearity and there is nothing to prove for this $B$; in the following steps take $B\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 034N, proof, second and third sentences; Tags 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring), and 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points)

proof.text: For the finite product $P=\prod_iK_i$ of step 2, define $\Phi:P\otimes_kA\to\prod_i(K_i\otimes_kA)$ by $\Phi((x_i)_i\otimes a)=(x_i\otimes a)_i$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] makes this a linear map, and the multiplication formula makes it a unital ring map. Let $\iota_i:K_i\to P$ insert a coordinate with zeros elsewhere, a $k$-linear map (it need not be unital). Define the additive inverse candidate by $\Psi((z_i)_i)=\sum_i(\iota_i\otimes1_A)(z_i)$. The identities $\pi_j\iota_i=0$ for $i\ne j$, $\pi_i\iota_i=1$, and $\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i=1_P$ give $\Phi\Psi=1$ and $\Psi\Phi=1$ on pure tensors, hence everywhere since pure tensors generate. Thus $\Phi$ is a ring isomorphism. The sum is finite; no assertion about commuting tensor products with an infinite product is used.

source.place: Tag 034N, proof, final two sentences: finite product of fields case, with the finite-product tensor identification written out

proof.text: For every $i$, the hypothesis applied to the field extension $K_i/k$ says $A\otimes_kK_i$ is reduced. The swap map $a\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes a$ is a ring isomorphism to $K_i\otimes_kA$, with inverse the same swap, by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the stated multiplication rule. Hence each $K_i\otimes_kA$ is reduced. A nilpotent tuple in their product has nilpotent, hence zero, coordinates, so that product is reduced; step 3 then makes $P\otimes_kA$ reduced. By step 1, $j\otimes1_A:B\otimes_kA\to P\otimes_kA$ is injective. A nilpotent in $B\otimes_kA$ maps to a nilpotent in the reduced target, hence to zero, and injectivity makes it zero. Therefore $B\otimes_kA$ is reduced for every finitely generated $k$-subalgebra $B\subseteq R$.

source.place: Tag 034N, proof, final sentence and descent through the product-of-fields embedding

proof.text: Let $z\in R\otimes_kA$ satisfy $z^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$. By the generation clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $z=\sum_{j=1}^m r_j\otimes a_j$ (scalar coefficients can be absorbed into the $r_j$). Let $B\subseteq R$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by these finitely many $r_j$, and put $z_B=\sum_j r_j\otimes a_j\in B\otimes_kA$. The map $B\otimes_kA\to R\otimes_kA$ sends $z_B$ to $z$ and is injective by step 1. It sends $z_B^n$ to zero, so $z_B^n=0$. Step 4 gives $z_B=0$, hence $z=0$. This proves reducedness for arbitrary $R$, without a finite-generation assumption on either algebra. Empty sums and the zero algebras give the zero tensor and satisfy the same conclusion.

source.place: Tag 034N, proof, first sentence, expanded using the finite tensor expression of Tag 00I3 (lemma-limit-argument)
